chapter: Cab Calloway, Harlem and New York musicians
title: Steele points out old performers, Lovie Joe and Rat Lovie Joe
summary: Steele taught Danny who was who in Harlem, including the old pimp and performer Lovie Joe.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: No. One of them kind of names. So he'd tell me all...you know, who was (?). And he'd see old performers, old musicians. He'd say "Do you see that woman? That woman..." I'm trying to think of this woman's name. He said, "That woman performed for the Tsar of Russia." She was a little dark woman. She was what you call... She did a whole lot of tumbling.
Some kind of... I can't think of that name. But he'd tell me... And he'd tell me who was who. And he'd

say "Lovie Joe. That's the great Lovie Joe." Lovie Joe was the star of the song that got(?) "Stop It, Joe." It's an old risqué tune that all the performers used to do. And Lovie Joe was supposed to have been an old-time Mack Man, an old-time pimp. Now, this is an old man, dark, with real keen features, and he looked like he's got blue eyes. Strange looking. And he's always on 135th Street, going into one bar, into another one, always dressed immaculate. He was about as big as me, slim, and... He said, "That's Lovie Joe." "What about him? What about him?" He said, "That's Lovie Joe." He said, "Now, they got Lovie Joe and they got Rat Lovie Joe." That's the way he talked. He said, "I'm gonna show you Rat Lovie Joe." So later on he showed me another cat, said...later on... He said, "That's Lovie Joe." He said, "He's been in and out of jail. But this man's has been classed(?). He's just livin' on his old reputation now."
That's the kind of cat Steele(?) was. He knew everybody, he'd get gigs, and call me on a gig, and we'd always meet and...
He was always... I always remember him because of you, and I was always around wherever I could find you, and he would be there, and he sort of accepted me and treated me very nicely.
